- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for mean reversion toward recent trend.
- Avoid overreacting to recent volatility; smooth out forecast peaks by reducing amplitude by 10–15% if preceded by a spike.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in subsequent days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict near the end of the horizon; apply a downward bias of 1–3% for the last 5–7 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in the first 10 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% for the first 5 days to align with historical mean reversion.
